title: May Admin Portal Pilot — Architecture Validation Results
status: PASS — 2 findings requiring design resolution, 0 blockers

role_architecture_validation.summary: 5-role hierarchical RBAC model is internally consistent. Roles escalate cleanly Level 1→5 with inheritance documented in both spec files. Two permission conflicts identified (System Admin vs. governance-guard rules, Governance Admin vs. Certification Reviewer override).

hierarchical_inheritance.design: Correct by design. Higher roles inherit all lower-role permissions. This is explicitly stated in both S203_ADMIN_PLATFORM_SPEC (authentication.mechanism) and S203_ROLE_MODEL (role_hierarchy.description).

governance_admin.description: Governance Admin inherits Certification Reviewer permissions including certify/hold/escalate. The spec states Governance Admin 'cannot override Certification Reviewer decisions'. However, hierarchical inheritance means Governance Admin has the same certify/hold/escalate capabilities as a Certification Reviewer — creating an ambiguous boundary. If two people with different roles both have certify permission, which one's decision binds?
governance_admin.recommendation: The authorization layer should implement a role-precedence rule: Certification Reviewer decisions on certify/hold/escalate are final for content quality; Governance Admin may only trigger these transitions for governance-enforcement reasons (e.g., quarantining a certified item with a newly discovered structural defect). The audit log must record which role initiated each state transition.

content_admin_governance_overlap.design: Correct. Content Admin → Certification Reviewer → Governance Admin is an intentional escalation chain. Governance Admin should have Content Admin permissions because they need full inventory visibility to perform registry integrity checks and framework control management.

permission_gaps.summary: 3 gaps identified. None are blockers for P0 but require P1/P2 resolution.

gaps.description: No role has explicit permission to archive a question (question_state → 'Archived'). The Certification Reviewer can certify/hold/escalate but archive is not listed. The governance model defines 'Archived' as a valid state but no role is assigned the transition authority.
gaps.recommendation: Add 'archive_items' to Certification Reviewer permissions in the role model.
gaps.current_workaround: Governance Admin 'authorize_state_transitions' may implicitly cover this.

gaps.description: No role has explicit permission to delete a recommendation. The Recommendation Registry module supports CRUD lifecycle (OPEN→ASSIGNED→IN_PROGRESS→CLOSED) but not deletion. This may be by design — recommendations are audit artifacts.
gaps.recommendation: If deletion is not intended, document this as a design decision. If it is intended, assign to Governance Admin (Level 4+).
gaps.current_workaround: CLOSE status effectively retires a recommendation without deletion.

gaps.description: No role has permission to edit Certified questions. Content Admin can only 'edit_unprocessed_content'. If a correctness defect (e.g., DL-030 answer-key error) is found in a Certified item, no role can directly fix it. The item must be transitioned back to In Audit first — but no role has explicit permission for Certified→In Audit re-verification transitions.
gaps.recommendation: Certification Reviewer should have explicit 'reopen_certified' permission to transition Certified→In Audit for re-verification (consistent with QUESTION_METADATA_STANDARD §9.2).
gaps.current_workaround: Governance Admin 'authorize_state_transitions' covers this implicitly but lacks the CAQS review expertise expected for re-verification.

system_admin_vs_governance.description: System Admin has 'all_permissions' (Level 5). The spec states System Admin 'cannot modify governance-guard rules without Governance Admin approval'. However, 'all_permissions' is unbounded — there is no mechanism defined to carve out governance-guard modification from System Admin scope. With Level 5 access, System Admin could directly edit `.opencode/plugins/governance-guard.js` (or the audit log at `knowledge/REVISION_HISTORY.md`) since all admin modules share the same data layer (architecture_notes.data_layer).
system_admin_vs_governance.enforcement_requirement: This constraint cannot be enforced by RBAC alone — it requires a write-gate at the governance-guard file level. The governance-guard plugin (Rules 2/3/5 BLOCK, Rules 1/4 WARN) operates at the OpenCode tooling layer, not at the admin portal frontend layer. The admin portal must implement an independent governance-guard modification gate that requires dual-role authorization (System Admin initiates, Governance Admin approves).
system_admin_vs_governance.resolution_required: Before S910 Phase 2 gate — the governance-guard.js file-level write-gate must be implemented independently of the admin portal RBAC.

module_architecture_validation.summary: 7 modules spec'd, 5 P0 + 3 P1. Architecture is coherent. One gap identified: case bank items are not explicitly scoped in Question Management module, and the data-source chain for certification queues may have staleness windows.

Question_Management.design_review: Comprehensive search by 7+ dimensions (QuestionID, identity key, domain, pack, section, state, defect class). View detail, certification history, linked sessions, linked recommendations.

scope_coverage.mcq_items: All 2,500 items across 5 packs (pack_*_corrected.js) — covered via CANONICAL_REGISTRY.json + AM-1 extraction.
scope_coverage.case_bank_items: FINDING M-204-01 (MEDIUM): The 420 case items across 75 cases (scored_cases*.js) are not explicitly scoped. The data_source field mentions CANONICAL_REGISTRY.json but does not clarify whether this includes case items. Case items use CBQ*-* IDs, not P1*-* IDs. The QuestionID search (compound-key resolved) should resolve both MCQ and case-item IDs.
scope_coverage.recommendation: Clarify in the Question Management module spec whether case-item IDs (CBQ*-*) are searchable. If yes, the CANONICAL_REGISTRY must include case items.

Recommendation_Registry.design_review: Full lifecycle: OPEN → ASSIGNED → IN_PROGRESS → CLOSED. Features cover status filtering, assignment, update, linkage to questions/sessions, closure evidence, creation from findings.
Recommendation_Registry.search_capability: The spec lists REC-ID search implicitly (filter by status implies lookup by ID). Add explicit 'Search by REC-ID' to the feature list for completeness.

Session_Registry.design_review: Search by session ID. View type, status, findings, deliverables, linked questions, linked recommendations, produced reports. Data source: NAVIGATION_REGISTRY.json + session report files.
Session_Registry.completeness: The link between sessions→recommendations and sessions→questions is the key architecture value. This enables traceability from any defect fix back to the session that identified it.

Certification_Operations_Console.design_review: 5 board queues (READY, MINOR_FIX, REMEDIATE, BLOCKED, CERTIFIED). Per-item CAQS 10-dimension review. Batch operations. Queue filtering by pack/section/defect class/priority.

queue_definitions_validated.READY: Items that passed all pre-flight gates. Maps to question_state: 'In Audit' with all 6-dimension AI verifications at HIGH confidence.
queue_definitions_validated.MINOR_FIX: SOFT_BLOCK warnings. Maps to items with DL-013 boilerplate or cosmetic metadata issues — not certification-blocking.
queue_definitions_validated.REMEDIATE: Items requiring defect remediation. Maps to items with DL-008, DL-026, or other structural defects.
queue_definitions_validated.BLOCKED: Items with structural impairments. Maps to items that cannot be parsed or have fundamental field-level corruption.
queue_definitions_validated.CERTIFIED: Items in learner delivery pool. Maps to question_state: 'Certified'.

Certification_Operations_Console.data_freshness: FINDING M-204-02 (LOW): CANONICAL_REGISTRY.json is generated at session T0 (architecture_notes.data_layer). If certification operations occur mid-session, the registry may be stale until the next session's T0. The Readiness Engine classification must either regenerate on-demand or the admin portal must document the staleness window.

Admin_Auth.design_review: 5-layer RBAC with access tokens managed via app.js session mechanism. Separate login for admin vs. student (admin.html vs. index_updated.html).
Admin_Auth.enforcement_points: Every module must check role at entry. Every write action must check permission at execution. Governance hooks write to REVISION_HISTORY.md on state transitions.

Student_Management.design_review: CRUD, enrollment management, permission assignment, progress tracking, study plan generation. Data source: Student database (future feature).

Test_Results.design_review: Search by student/date/exam/question. Score distribution analytics. Per-question performance stats. Data source: app.js localStorage / future server-side storage.
Test_Results.concern: localStorage is client-side only — no centralized results database exists. Until server-side storage is implemented, results analytics will only show data from the local browser.
Test_Results.status: DESIGN_PASS — gated by server-side storage implementation

Modernization_Dashboard.design_review: Domain E/F modernization, seed inventory, clone archival, replacement tracking, certification by section, defect escape rate, throughput metrics (BF-001 through BF-010), phase gate status (S830/S900/S910).
Modernization_Dashboard.data_sources_validated: CANONICAL_REGISTRY.json + DELTA_LEDGER.json + scan artifacts + throughput metrics. All sources exist or are spec'd for generation at session T0.

permission_boundary_validation.summary: All 5 roles have verified boundaries. 2 findings on enforcement mechanisms.

Student.enforcement: Session-scoped query. app.js session object contains only the authenticated student's data. Test results, reviews, and recommendations are filtered by student ID at query time.

Content_Admin.rule: Can view all questions but only edit Unprocessed content
Content_Admin.enforcement: Read: all question_states visible. Write: edit_unprocessed_content permission gates writes to question_state !== 'Unprocessed'. The ROLE_MODEL permission_catalog confirms edit_unprocessed is restricted to Unprocessed state.
Content_Admin.edge_case: If a Content Admin attempts to edit a Certified item: the write gate must reject the operation and log the attempt. Currently no explicit mechanism defined for this gate — it relies on the question_state field check at the data layer.

Certification_Reviewer.rule: Can certify/hold/escalate but not delete questions
Certification_Reviewer.enforcement: Certification Reviewer has certify/hold/escalate permissions (permission_catalog.certification). No delete permission exists in the catalog for any role below Level 5. The deletion prohibition is enforced by permission absence, which is the correct RBAC pattern.

Governance_Admin.rule: Can manage rules but not override Certification Reviewer decisions
Governance_Admin.enforcement: This is the F-204-01 finding. Governance Admin inherits certify/hold/escalate via hierarchy, creating ambiguity. Resolution: implement a role-precedence rule where Certification Reviewer decisions on content quality are final. Governance Admin transitions must carry a distinct audit reason code.
Governance_Admin.verdict: PASS_WITH_CONDITION — enforcement mechanism must be designed before S830

System_Admin.rule: Full access but cannot modify governance-guard rules without Governance Admin approval
System_Admin.enforcement: This is the F-204-02 finding. RBAC alone cannot enforce this — requires a dual-authorization gate at the governance-guard file level. Until implemented, System Admin has de facto governance-guard modification capability.
System_Admin.verdict: PASS_WITH_CONDITION — enforcement mechanism must be designed before S910

require_design_resolution: F-204-01 (Governance Admin vs. Certification Reviewer override — MEDIUM)
F-204-02 (System Admin vs. governance-guard rules — HIGH)
M-204-01 (Case bank items in Question Management — MEDIUM)

governance_guard_rules.admin_portal_integration: Certification Operations Console must enforce Rule 2 (BLOCK) at certify time — no item with non-empty ExplanationWrong[CorrectChoice] may transition to Certified. The console's write hooks to REVISION_HISTORY.md satisfy Rule 1 (WARN) pairing requirement.

state_transition_logging.mechanism: Certification Operations Console writes to REVISION_HISTORY.md on state transitions (architecture_notes.governance_hooks).
state_transition_logging.completeness: The hook covers state transitions. It should also log: (a) role that initiated the transition, (b) timestamp, (c) affected QIDs, (d) reason code.
state_transition_logging.recommendation: Add structured fields to REVISION_HISTORY entries: {role, timestamp, qids[], reason_code, before_state, after_state}.

open_defects.DL-008: 67 Certified items with non-empty EW[CC] — highest learner-safety priority
open_defects.DL-026: 50 In Audit items with empty distractor slots

pre_existing_state_reference.implication_for_admin_portal: The BLOCKED queue in Certification Operations Console must pre-populate with these 67 DL-008 items. The REMEDIATE queue must include the 50 DL-026 items. Both queues must reference the defect manifest at governance/DEFECT_MANIFEST_DL008_DL026.json.
